strategy.summary: Small founder-owned turning shop (25 staff), our long-standing main source (70% quota since 2011) for pump shaft HN 24 mm in 1.4404. It is financially sound but thin, now capacity-tight after winning a large hydraulics contract, and it asks for faster payment and binding 12-month volume. The price has been cut repeatedly and sits at or slightly below our should-cost (25.22 vs 24.92, error about 5%). Drivers rose over 12 months (bars, labour, alloy) but have softened since June. Delivery (75.9% OTD) and quality (921 ppm, twice the peer median) are weak but improving versus a year ago. Our late payment is a sore point. Room on price is little: we should hold near the current price by trading cash, binding volume and length, not by squeezing.

findings.text: Price sits at or slightly below full cost: current EUR 24.92 vs should-cost EUR 25.22 (no margin included), i.e. -1.2%. Confidence is only ±5%, so the true gap ranges from roughly -6% to +4%. There is little room to push price down on cost grounds, and the supplier can credibly claim it earns no margin on this part.

Cost drivers rose over the last 12 months. The weighted effect is about +3.9% on price: labour +2.7% (weight 0.33), cold-drawn bars +12.3% (0.19), alloy surcharge 1.4404 +5.9% (0.12) and power -3.7% (0.01). These drivers cover only about 65% of cost. The supplier has a checkable case for an increase of roughly 3-4%.

Recent momentum is softening. Cold-drawn bars are -2.3% since their 2026-06 peak, and the alloy surcharge fell -5.5% from 2026-06 to 2026-09. Labour is flat at its peak. Together this caps the claim at roughly -1.1% off the 12-month figure.

Price history runs 26.37 (2023), 25.67 (2024), 25.67 (2025), then 24.92 from 2026-01, a cumulative cut of -5.5%. That cut came while bar and labour costs were rising, so the last renewal (-2.9%) left it below cost.

Competing prices: the second source, sup:70210, is billed at EUR 24.37 (-2.2% vs this supplier), which is below should-cost too. In the 2025-06 benchmark RFQ, Rottaler quoted 27.00 against Dralveck's 26.00, yet Rottaler won the award. Both quotes are over a year old and below 2026 prices, so they are weak anchors.

Room on price is thin. A realistic landing zone is a hold at 24.92 up to about +2-3% (25.4-25.7, close to the standard price of 25.4). We would get there by trading for things it values rather than arguing cost: faster payment, a binding 12-month volume of 14,650, or a longer term. It has asked for both faster payment and volume commitment in writing.

findings.text: Small founder-owned shop (25 staff, turnover 2-5 M EUR). The founder/owner almost certainly decides personally; there is no visible approval ladder. Finances are stable but thin: equity ratio 21.7%, credit index 231 and unchanged over 12 months. It is not distressed and can afford to walk away.

Capacity is now tight. A multi-year hydraulics contract occupies most of its turning capacity from summer 2026. It has twice written, in identical words, that additional volume is confirmed only against a binding 12-month commitment. We are likely being deprioritised for extra volume. Commitment length and binding volume are the currency it values.

It wants cash. It asked us to pay within 10 days in exchange for a cash discount. Our payment record is poor and a real sensitivity: 94.4% of invoices paid late, 10.4 days late on average, 50% more than 10 days late, max 23. Faster or on-time payment is a cheap concession with high value to it. It can also be a complaint used against us.

Its style is terse and transactional: short e-mails with repeated boilerplate and no expressed grievances on price. Historically it settles well below its ask (3 renewals: asked +0.8% on average, settled -1.9%), and its price has fallen 5.5% since 2023. It has not used rising costs much so far, but that may change now that its capacity is full.

Weaknesses in its position:
- Delivery is 75.9% on time against a 95% target.
- Quality is 921 ppm against a peer median of 457.
- We own the tooling and have an approved second source (Dralveck, 30% quota, currently cheaper at 24.37).
- Our spend is about 6.3% of its turnover.

Counterweight: its should-cost model shows it selling about 1.2% below cost. Stability matters if the part is strategic.

Red flags:
- Capacity is absorbed by a larger customer.
- The price is fixed per calendar year; changes need notice 90 days before year end, so expect a notice around end of September 2026.
- The contract auto-renews unless terminated by 2027-04-01.

The evidence on people and decision-makers is thin: only 4 short e-mails exist, and there are no call or meeting notes.

findings.text: Framework contract runs 2025-07-01 to 2027-06-30 and extends by 12 months unless terminated with 90 days' notice. To stop the renewal, notice is due by 2027-04-01, so a credible exit remains open.

Prices are fixed per calendar year. Any change for 2027 needs written notice at least 90 days before year end, i.e. by about 2026-10-02. Absent timely notice, the current EUR 24.92 stays fixed through 2026. Payment terms are 30 days net, below our 60-day standard, which already favours the supplier. Delivery is EXW with a 35-day lead time.

The quality agreement sets a 95% on-time target and a EUR 150 flat fee per supplier-caused complaint. The supplier misses the target badly: 75.9% on time, and 921 ppm against a peer median of 457 ppm. It has 8 complaints on this part, with EUR 900 recharged.

Settlement history: over 3 renewals it asked +0.8% on average and settled at -1.9%, a gap of about 2.7 pp. When it asked +3.7% for 2025, it settled at 0. Its asks are soft and it moves materially below them. The price has fallen from 26.37 (2023) to 24.92 (2026).

Dependency is moderate and two-sided. We hold 70% quota with this supplier, and sup:70210 holds 30% at a lower price of EUR 24.37. We own the tooling, so the part can be shifted. Our spend is about 6.3% of its turnover. However, it has won a large hydraulics contract that fills most of its turning capacity, which lowers its need for our volume. Its should-cost is 25.22, above its price, which limits further cuts.

findings.text: Delivery is well below the 95% target but has recovered: rolling 12m OTD 75.9% vs requested (79.3% vs confirmed), up from a trough of 61.5% a year earlier. It is still below the peers' median of 84.6%. When it is late, it is late on average 13 days (max 32). The 2026Q2 peak of 80.8% slipped back in Q3, around the time the hydraulics contract started taking turning capacity in summer.

Quality improved from 1620 ppm (2024Q4) to a low of 592 ppm (2025Q4), then worsened again to 921 ppm in 2026Q3. That is about twice the peers' median of 457 ppm. All QNs concern part 320010, almost all supplier-caused. Recurring defects are surface damage, porosity, leakage, wrong certificate and burrs. One 8D is still open: qn:20005019 has no d8 date. 8D closure has often taken 2-3 months.

Defect costs are only partly recovered. About half of the QNs carried the EUR 150 fee; many supplier-caused QNs were recharged 0 (e.g. qn:20004965, qn:20004792, qn:20004668). The contract fee covers little of our real cost of defects and late delivery.

Volume outlook is rising. The shared 2026-09 forecast is 14650 pcs for the next 12 months against 12400 ordered in the last 12 months. Rottaler holds about 70% of the part (9050 pcs last 12m vs 3520 at sup:70210). The supplier has twice asked for a binding 12-month commitment, so firm volume is a currency we can trade.

Price: we pay 24.92 now, down from 26.37 in 2023. The second source sup:70210 is at 24.37 but has worse ppm (1882) on smaller lots. Recent POs are confirmed on the requested date, so current lead times are being met.

Several records argue the supplier's case. Its price is about 1% below the should-cost (EUR 25.22), and the cold-drawn bar index rose 12.3% in 12 months. The hydraulics contract fills its capacity, which reduces its need for our volume. We also pay late: 94% of invoices, about 10 days on average.

arguments.text: Our price already sits below a margin-free cost of making the part. Your own should-cost for this shaft is 25.22 EUR before any margin, and we invoice 24.92. After cuts of -2.7 % and -2.9 % in two of the last three renewals, a further cut is not sustainable. A hold is the floor, and a modest increase is justified.

Our cost drivers rose over the last twelve months: cold-drawn bar +12.3 %, labour +2.7 % and the 1.4404 alloy surcharge +5.9 %. Bar alone is about a fifth of our cost. That roughly covers a 3-4 % increase.

You pay late on almost every invoice: 94.4 % paid late, about 10 days on average and up to 23 days. For a small shop with 21.7 % equity this costs us real money. It is part of why we cannot absorb more cuts.
Our capacity is now largely booked by a multi-year hydraulics contract. We can reserve capacity for Hollerau, including your forecast growth to 14,650 pcs, only against a binding 12-month commitment.
Our quality is clearly better than your second source: 921 ppm against 1,882. We have supplied this part since 2011, and our ppm has improved from about 1,600 in 2024.

weak_points: Our on-time delivery is 75.9 % against a 95 % target and slipped again in Q3; Hollerau could argue that capacity is going to the hydraulics customer.
There are still 8 complaints a year, and a coating complaint from 2026-09 has no 8D closed yet.
Dralveck is cheaper at 24.37 and could take more of our 70 % quota.
Bar is down 2.3 % and the alloy surcharge down 5.5 % from their June peaks; power is falling; we asked -1.2 % ourselves last year.
Our price must be notified 90 days before year end per clause 3.1, so timing is tight for a 2027 increase.
The should-cost carries about 5 % uncertainty, so 'below cost' is not proven.
We need this volume more than we admit, since we are a 25-person shop.
wants: On-time payment, or payment within 10-14 days against a cash discount of about 1-2 %; this is our top trade.
A binding 12-month volume of about 13,000-14,500 pcs, keeping or raising our 70 % quota.
Price held at 24.92, or a +2-3 % increase if payment terms stay as they are.
An index clause on the 1.4404 alloy surcharge or on bar, if we must accept a fixed price for longer.
A longer lead time of 42 days to fit our capacity.
red_lines: No extra volume without a binding commitment.
No raise in the chargeback above 150 EUR per complaint, and no strict ppm commitment, without a price adjustment.
No multi-year fixed price without either an index clause or payment improvement.
red_team.opening: Thank Hollerau for the long partnership since 2011 and point to our quality advantage. Then state plainly that after repeated cuts our price is below your own margin-free should-cost while bar, labour and alloy have risen. Ask +3.9 % from 1 January 2027, or a hold at 24.92 if Hollerau commits to payment within 14 days (or on time with a 2 % discount), a binding 12-month volume of about 14,000 pcs, and a 24-month extension. Offer to reserve capacity and commit to an OTD improvement plan in return.

rebuttals.answer: We respect that the price has come down over the years and we are not asking for a further cut; but our estimate carries a wide margin of error, so it shows the price is close to cost, not below it. Your own renewal history shows you have repeatedly settled below your ask, and today's price is the anchor we would like to hold, supported by volume, length and payment rather than by a higher unit price.

The twelve-month rises are real and we take them seriously, but weighted by their share of your cost they add up to far less than the increase you mention. Bar and the alloy surcharge have both eased since their recent peaks, and power has fallen, so the trend going into next year is softer than the twelve-month view suggests.

You are right, our payment has not been on time and we are sorry for that. We will commit to paying on the agreed date, and we are open to discussing faster payment against the cash discount you offered, as a separate trade rather than as a price increase.

We understand the new contract fills your lathes, and we are prepared to give the binding commitment you asked for, within our forecast need and over a longer term. In return we need that reserved capacity to show up in on-time delivery, which is still well short of the agreed target and slipped again recently.
We value the long partnership and the clear improvement in your quality over the past two years.

press: We would like the capacity you reserve for us to be reflected in delivery performance, which still sits well below the target in our quality agreement.
Since bar and alloy surcharge have both eased since early summer, we would expect any cost discussion to reflect that softer trend.
As our framework agreement fixes prices per calendar year with written notice before year end, we would be glad to agree the terms for next year together in good time.
We would welcome a ppm commitment alongside the binding volume, so that both sides gain planning security.
